Thus, both races are relatively young and better educated. If present non-Indian population trends continue, improvements in intercultural relations will likely occur. Mixed marriages are not uncommon and in general, over the years the Indian and non-Indian residents have developed a rather accommodating, if not cordial relationship.
Jurisdictional Issues
The Crow Tribe feels it has overall jurisdiction within the interior boundaries of the reservation. Some conflicts and differences of opinion regarding jurisdiction still exist where the non-Indian and the state are concerned. There have been reasonable, if informal, accommodations developed over the past six decades between the various interests.
The law and order system, which is essential to the orderly growth and development of any community, is a good example of this accommodation. Presently, law enforcement people from tribal, county, state and federal levels are cross-deputized and function in a cooperative effort to maintain law and order.
Although the determination of jurisdiction is not entirely clear within the boundaries of the reservation, the only major dispute has involved fishing and hunting rights.
